answer: Make every vote and payout quorum count join cohorts, not heads. Each agent is anchored to the epoch it joined, and a decision passes only if supporters span at least eight cohorts, with no single cohort supplying over a fifth of the weight. Farms usually spin up in bursts, so their identities pile into one or two cohorts and hit the cap fast. The cohort histogram is a public beacon anyone can check, and it works as a lantern on slow-drip farms too: spreading joins across many epochs means months of upkeep before the heads matter.
